stem.text: Let \( f(x) = 7 \ln\left(1 + \frac{x - 2}{1}\right) \). The Taylor series for f about \( x = 2 \) is \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{7 (-1)^{n+1} \left(x - 2\right)^{n}}{n \cdot 1^{n}} \). Its radius of convergence is \( 1 \). Does the series converge to f at \( x = 1 \)? Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: No, because \( x = 1 \) is an endpoint that the interval of convergence \( 1 < x \le 3 \) excludes.

worked_solution.text: The ratio test gives convergence for \( \left|x - 2\right| < 1 \), the interior \( 1 < x < 3 \), and \( x = 1 \) is an endpoint.
At \( x = 1 \) the series is \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{-7}{n} \), a multiple of the harmonic series, which diverges, so the interval of convergence is \( 1 < x \le 3 \).
No, because \( x = 1 \) is an endpoint that the interval of convergence \( 1 < x \le 3 \) excludes.
